key_insight: Glass panels for transistor-written IGZO gain-cell tiers (endurance unlimited), with sensing moved to mass-transferred Si chiplets, which avoids slow, variable TFT sense amps.
killer_doubt: At ~$100-150/m2 per TFT tier, 32 tiers at F=0.3 um (16F2 cell) is ~$2.4/GB, above DDR5's $1.48. 10x needs F~0.1 um, ~30 nm overlay on glass.
decisive_experiment: On a Gen-2/4.5 display R&D line, stack 4 IGZO 2T0C tiers at 0.5 um. Measure per-tier D0/yield, tier-to-tier overlay after glass compaction, 85 C retention, and read latency through 2 mm RDL bitlines.
prior_art: Phase B N-38 (panel 3D oxide memory) and N-36 (glass carriers); SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM; X-Celeprint micro-transfer printing of Si chiplets.

key_insight: Pre-latch charge gain is the right lever: ~5x gain before the latch would let Cs fall from ~5 fF to ~1 fF and shorten the pillar ~4x.
killer_doubt: EMCCD stages give ~1-1.5% gain at ~40 V clocks. 1.2x per stage means near-breakdown fields, exponential V/T gain spread, hot-carrier aging, and +10-50 ns tRCD.
decisive_experiment: 28-65 nm MPW: 10-stage high-field transfer-gate register. Measure gain per stage vs clock voltage, gain sigma across 1,000 registers, and gain decay after ~1e12 e- of throughput. ~$300k.
prior_art: EMCCD (e2v L3Vision, TI Impactron); DRAM charge-transfer pre-sensing; short or segmented bitlines (Phase B N-40, N-04) get the same Cs cut at 1 V.

key_insight: Compressed rows raise useful bits per activation, cutting activation energy per value. The HBM4 logic base die, not DRAM-process periphery, is the natural home.
killer_doubt: 4:1 quantization is the application's choice, not a memory gain. Lossless gain on dense int4 weights is ~1.1-1.3x, on activations ~1.5-2x. Decompressing before the I/O saves no link pJ/bit.
decisive_experiment: In software, trace LLM weights, KV cache and activations in production formats and measure the lossless row-granular ratio net of metadata. If below 1.5x for weights plus KV, stop. ~$50k.
prior_art: IBM MXT; LCP (MICRO 2013); Compresso (MICRO 2018); Buddy Compression (ISCA 2020); ZeroPoint Technologies compression IP; Samsung HBM-PIM, SK hynix AiM.

key_insight: Synchronized predictors at both ends of a link send only residuals, a cheap FPGA-demonstrable way to buy link bandwidth.
killer_doubt: Interleaved multi-stream traffic defeats per-line last-value and stride prediction. Realistic saving is ~1.2-1.5x of link bits, and the link is only part of access energy. Coding adds ~2-5 ns.
decisive_experiment: Replay published server and AI memory traces through the predictor pair in software and measure residual entropy. If the bit saving is below 1.5x, stop. ~$30k.
prior_art: Base-Delta-Immediate (PACT 2012), FPC, DBI bus encoding in DDR4/GDDR, NVIDIA compute data compression, link-compression literature.

key_insight: Self-limited charge sharing onto a ~0.2 fF node takes only Cn/(Cs+Cn)~4% of the charge but gives a ~0.48 V swing: near-non-destructive 64 B reads with no restore.
killer_doubt: Subthreshold sip: sigma Vt ~40-50 mV at ~90 mV/dec gives ~50x charge spread. The self-limited fix needs a local amplifier every ~3-8 cells. WL toggling still hammers.
decisive_experiment: 65-28 nm MPW: 5 fF MIM 1T1C cells on 0.2-1 fF local nodes with source-follower readout. Measure swing, charge loss per read, reads before restore and spread over 10k cells at 25-85 C. ~$400k.
prior_art: Hierarchical and local-bitline sensing; selective bitline activation (Udipi, ISCA 2010); gain cells (inherently non-destructive); Phase B N-40 MSB-DRAM.

key_insight: Every 2026 next-gen DRAM demo already bonds a periphery wafer to the cell wafer. An open per-segment interface lets litho-light cell fabs and US logic foundries split the value chain.
killer_doubt: At 40 nm BL pitch, 128-cell segments need <=0.45 um bonds, beyond production. W2W has no known-good die (0.9x0.9=0.81). Periphery must match each array's Cs, Cbl, ~3 V VPP.
decisive_experiment: Draft an electrical envelope spec. Tape out a 28/22 nm SA plus WL-driver periphery test chip and bond it at 1-2 um pitch to an IGZO or MIM-cap array wafer. Measure sense margin vs bond parasitics. ~$900k.
prior_art: Samsung VCT periphery-under-cell and SK hynix 4F2 VG (in-house bonding); YMTC Xtacking and Kioxia CBA for NAND; UCIe (die-level only). No open bitline-level standard found.

key_insight: Silicon-proven open SA-offset calibration, pumps and hammer trackers on US 22/28 nm would lower entry cost for bonded-periphery or BEOL oxide-cell entrants.
killer_doubt: The moat is process and yield learning (~1e-9 bit-fail tails), not circuits. Logic-wafer SAs apply only to bonded or BEOL-cell dies. The $500M to $50-100M saving is unsupported.
decisive_experiment: Tape out an offset-calibrated SA bank against MIM-cap bitline loads, a VPP pump and a PRAC-style counter on a US 22/28 nm MPW. Publish measured offset sigma and pump efficiency. ~$600k.
prior_art: OpenRAM (SRAM); OpenGCRAM (Stanford 2025, gain cell); LiteDRAM (controller and PHY). No open on-die DRAM periphery library found.

key_insight: Minimal-periphery 3T gain-cell macros on open US PDKs are cheap to prove and could seed a domestic memory-design base.
killer_doubt: Already exists as OpenGCRAM. At 130-180 nm a 3T cell is ~1-2 um2, under ~1 Mb/mm2, so one GB needs ~8,600 mm2: no effect on the RAM supply.
decisive_experiment: Port OpenGCRAM to SKY130/GF180, then measure 85 C retention and refresh power on one shuttle. If density is not 2x SRAM with refresh included, stop. ~$100k.
prior_art: OpenGCRAM (Stanford, arXiv 2507.10849, via search snippet), built on OpenRAM; RAAAM commercial 3T gain-cell compiler.

key_insight: Redox plateaus are intrinsic, identical references. Coating the reference electrode with the same molecules is a clever self-calibration for multi-level sensing.
killer_doubt: A 4F2 cell (F=20 nm) holds ~1,600 molecules, ~230 e- per level at 3 bits. 50 fF needs ~200x surface area. Solid counter-ions at >=1e8 redox/s are unshown.
decisive_experiment: Graft a ferrocene/porphyrin mix on porous TiN under a solid or ionic-gel electrolyte. Measure redox completion at 10-100 ns pulses, 1e10 cycles, and level separation after 400 C. ~$300k.
prior_art: ZettaCore (2000s); Liu et al., Science 2003, porphyrin memory surviving processing (training knowledge); Phase B N-17 (ALIVE-SPECULATIVE) is the re-scoped version.

key_insight: Bloom-filter weak-row lists with re-testing for variable retention can cut refresh ~4x with no die change. The value is licensable RTL.
killer_doubt: VRT and data-pattern dependence create new weak cells after profiling, and retention halves per ~10 C. DDR5 on-die ECC and remapping hide fail bits. Standard REF cannot skip rows.
decisive_experiment: On DRAM Bender with 20 DDR5 DIMMs, profile at 85 C, then run 256 ms refresh for 30 days with ECC logging and count escapes per GB-day. ~$150k.
prior_art: RAIDR (ISCA 2012, Bloom filters), AVATAR (DSN 2015), REAPER (ISCA 2017), BEER/HARP on-die-ECC profiling (MICRO 2020/2021).

key_insight: Strong LDPC behind a CXL buffer tolerates bit-fail densities that fail JEDEC bins, and ~us latency is acceptable in a capacity tier.
killer_doubt: Rejects are mostly gross, periphery, IDD or speed fails, and redundancy already fixes scattered bits. At ~85-90% yield only ~1-3% of bits are recoverable. 1% bad is ~1.6e8 bits, clustered.
decisive_experiment: Buy 1,000 rejected or eTT dies through a broker and map fail bits on an FPGA tester. If fewer than 30% show scattered fails that LDPC corrects at <1% overhead, stop. ~$150k.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek (off-spec component brand); UTT/eTT downgraded-DRAM market; DDR5 PPR; I-07272 (subarray retirement, other batch).

key_insight: Differential sensing against a matched reference pillar is the right instinct for selectorless arrays. Core memory's sense-wire weaving is a genuinely lost trick.
killer_doubt: Sneak current depends on data in ~31 half-selected cells per pillar, so at ON/OFF 10-100 twin mismatch exceeds the signal. RRAM/PCM endurance 1e6-1e9 vs 3e8-7e13 needed.
decisive_experiment: Monte Carlo SPICE of a 32-plane vertical RRAM pillar pair with measured ON/OFF spread and random data. If sense margin is below 3 sigma, stop. ~$20k.
prior_art: Vertical RRAM (Stanford Wong group, Samsung); complementary resistive switches (Linn et al., Nat. Mater. 2010); reference-column sneak cancellation schemes.
